Rashi on Megillah 28a:10:1.hebrew: גווזי - סריסין היו, עבדים משרתים אותו; וקא מחו ליה לר"ע, סבורין היו שהיה קץ בחייו:
Rashi on Megillah 28a:10:1.english: Gavzei - They were eunuchs, servants who attended him; and they were beating Rabbi Akiva [because] they thought that he was impatient with his [Rabbi Nechunya's] life:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:10:2.hebrew: אם נאמר כבש - "את הכבש אחד תעשה בבקר":
Rashi on Megillah 28a:10:2.english: If it is stated "lamb" - [This refers to the verse:] "The one lamb you shall offer in the morning" [Numbers 28:4]:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:12:1.english: Nor did I stand on my measures - [that is,] to repay evil to one who distressed me:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:15:1.english: I need to learn - perhaps I will be able to fulfill [it]:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:15:2.english: Were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, I would not look toward you, nor see you - Elisha said this to Jehoram:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:19:1.hebrew: הבאים אחריך בהמה ירעו - בתמיה: אין טוב לך לחיות ימים רבים כמוני, שא"כ לא יטלו בניך בגדולתך, ואתה נשיא, והם כל ימיהם יהיו הדיוטות:
Rashi on Megillah 28a:19:1.english: Shall those who come after you tend cattle - [This is said] in astonishment: It is not good for you to live as many days as I [did], for if so, your sons will not partake in your greatness — you [will remain] Nasi, and they, all their days, will be commoners:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:1:1.english: Its [priestly] portions - the foreleg, the jaws, and the maw:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:1:2.hebrew: ולא ברכתי - בסעודה לפני כהן, דאמר מר (גיטין דף נט:): "וקדשתו" (ויקרא כא) — לכל דבר שבקדושה, לפתוח ראשון ולברך ראשון:
Rashi on Megillah 28a:1:2.english: And I never recited [a blessing] - [meaning] at a meal in the presence of a priest, as the Master said (Gittin 59b): "You shall sanctify him" (Leviticus 21) — [applying] to every matter of sanctity: to open [reading the Torah] first, and to recite the blessing [over the meal] first:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:21:2.english: Without Torah - My [Torah] study was always fluent in my mouth:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:21:3.english: (By his nickname [ḥanikhato]) - [That is,] if [people] gave his fellow a derogatory name.

Rashi on Megillah 28a:21:4.hebrew: ואמרי לה (בחכינתו) - אפילו אותו כינוי שמסודר ובא לו ממשפחתו, שם דופי, כמו "כתב חניכתו וחניכתה" דמסכת גיטין (דף פז:):
Rashi on Megillah 28a:21:4.english: And some say (by his nickname [bachakhinato]) - [This refers to] even that nickname that is established and comes down to him from his family — a name of reproach — like [the phrase] "he wrote his family nickname and her family nickname" [ketav chanikhato vechanikhatah] of Tractate Gittin (87b):

Rashi on Megillah 28a:22:1.hebrew: מפשילין חבלים - והוא הדין לכל מלאכות, אלא לפי שהפשלת חבלים צריך מקום מרווח פנוי, ובית הכנסת גדול הוא וראוי ומספיק לכך:
Rashi on Megillah 28a:22:1.english: Stretch out ropes - And the same law [applies] to all [other] types of work; [the Mishnah specifies this] only because stretching out ropes requires a wide, open space, and a synagogue is large and suitable and sufficient for that:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:24:1.hebrew: מפני עגמת נפש - מניחין בו עשבים כדי שתהא עגמת נפש לרואיהן, ושיזכירו את ימי בניינו ואת שהיו רגילין להתאסף שם, יבקשו רחמים שיחזרו לקדמותו:
Rashi on Megillah 28a:24:1.english: Due to anguish - They leave grass in it so that there will be anguish for those who see it, and [when] they remember the days of its building and that they used to gather there, they will beseech mercy that they return to its former state:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:25:1.hebrew: אין אוכלין בהן כו' - ולא גרסינן "ואין אוכלין בהן", דכולהו פירושא דקלות ראש הן — לשון קלות, שמקילין אותה:
Rashi on Megillah 28a:25:1.english: One may not eat in them, etc. - And we do not read "and one may not eat in them" [with the prefix "and"], because all of them are an explanation of "frivolity" — an expression of lightness, [meaning] that they treat it [the synagogue] lightly:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:4:1.hebrew: משניאי - שגורמין לבני אדם לשנאותו, שהרואה תלמיד חכם שפל לפני עם הארץ, אומר: אין נחת רוח בתורה:
Rashi on Megillah 28a:4:1.english: Those who make Me hated [masni'ai] - [Meaning] those who cause people to hate Him, for one who sees a Torah scholar humbled before an ignoramus says, "There is no satisfaction in Torah."

Rashi on Megillah 28a:6:1.english: I never attained honor, etc. - [the Gemara] goes on to explain it:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:7:1.english: Mara [a hoe] - forés [a spade or hoe] in Old French:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:7:2.english: And he was taking [it] from him - to honor him, so that he [himself] would carry it:

Rashi on Megillah 28a:7:3.english: You carry in your city - [Meaning,] that you carry a tool like this in your city:

Tosafot on Megillah 28a:20:1.hebrew: תיתי לי דלא עבדי שותפות עם הכותי - אפי' בענין שאינו יכול לבא לידי שבועה, ואפילו יחול עליו שבועה יפטרנו, דשרי בשאר בני אדם, אפ"ה לא היה רוצה לעשות:
Tosafot on Megillah 28a:20:1.english: May [a blessing] come to me for I never formed a partnership with a Kuti - Even in a case where he cannot come to [the point of] an oath, and even [if] an oath should fall upon him he would exempt him — which is permitted for other people — even so, he did not want to do [so]:

Tosafot on Megillah 28a:22:1.hebrew: ועוד א"ר יהודה: בית הכנסת שחרב - קשה, מאי "ועוד"? דהא לעיל הוה מקיל טפי מחכמים, והכא הוא מחמיר, ואם כן מאי "ועוד"? וי"ל, דקאי אהא דאמר ר' יהודה ברישא: מוכרין אותו לשם חצר — ודוקא לשם חצר קאמר, אבל סתם אינה יורדת מקדושתה; והיינו "ועוד" דאמר ר' יהודה, כלומר: ועוד חומרא אחרת מלבד הראשונה:
Tosafot on Megillah 28a:22:1.english: And Rabbi Yehuda said further: A synagogue that fell into ruin - [This is] difficult: what is [the meaning of] "and further"? For earlier [Rabbi Yehuda] was more lenient than the Sages, whereas here he is stringent; and if so, what is [meant by] "and further"? And one can say that it refers to that which Rabbi Yehuda said in the first clause: "they sell it as a courtyard" — and specifically "as a courtyard" did he say [that it may be sold], but without specification it does not descend from its sanctity; and this is [the meaning of] "and further" that Rabbi Yehuda said, meaning: and further, another stringency besides the first one:

Tosafot on Megillah 28a:25:1.hebrew: אין אוכלין ואין שותין בהן - והא דאמר בריש ערבי פסחים (פסחים דף קא. ושם) דאורחין אכלו ושתו בבי כנישתא, רוצה לומר בחדר הסמוכה לבית הכנסת:
Tosafot on Megillah 28a:25:1.english: One may not eat nor drink in them - And as for that which [the Gemara] says at the beginning of [the chapter] Arvei Pesachim (Pesachim 101a and there), that guests ate and drank in the synagogue — it means in a room adjacent to the synagogue:

Tosafot on Megillah 28a:5:1.hebrew: כי קאמר איהו בשוין - וקשה: מאי רבותא? והא כתיב "וקדשתו" — לכל דבר שבקדושה, לברך ראשון! וי"ל ד"שוין" לאו דוקא, אלא כלומר שהכהן נמי תלמיד חכם, אמנם אינו חשוב כמותו, ואפי' הכי לא היה רבי פרידא רוצה לקרות לפניו. וגם צריך לומר דשאר כהנים היו כפופים לרבי פרידא, דאל"כ לא הוי רבותא, כדחזינן פרק הניזקין (גיטין דף נט. ושם), דרב הונא לא הוי קרי בכהני אי לאו דרבי אמי ורבי אסי, כהני חשיבי דארעא דישראל, הוו כייפי ליה. ועי"ל דהא דאמר התם דרב הונא לא הוה קרי בכהני אלא משום דשאר כהני כייפו ליה, היינו דווקא בשבתות וי"ט דאיכא כינופיא, אבל בב' ובה' קורא שפיר בפני כהן, אע"ג דלא הוי גדול כ"כ, וכדיוקא זה יש בהדיא פרק הניזקין; ורבי פרידא לא רצה לקרות בפני כהן אפילו בב' ובה'. ורש"י פירש דהכא מיירי בברכת המזון, וה"נ משמע לישנא ד"לא ברכתי", מדלא קאמר "ולא קריתי", וברכת המזון לא נתקן להן משום דרכי שלום, ואפי' הכי לא היה רוצה רבי פרידא לברך בפני הכהן:
Tosafot on Megillah 28a:5:1.english: When he says [this, it is] of equals - And it is difficult: what is the novelty? Surely it is written, "And you shall sanctify him" — [meaning] for every matter of sanctity, to bless first! And one can say that "equals" is not [meant] literally; rather, it means that the kohen is also a Torah scholar, though he is not as distinguished as him, and even so Rabbi Perida did not want to read [the Torah] before him. And one must also say that the other kohanim were subordinate to Rabbi Perida, for if not, it would not be a novelty — as we see in the chapter [entitled] HaNizakin (Gittin 59a and there), that Rav Huna would not have read [in the portion of] the kohanim were it not that Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi, the distinguished kohanim of the Land of Israel, deferred to him. And one can further say that what it says there, that Rav Huna would not have read [in the portion of] the kohanim except because the other kohanim deferred to him, applies specifically on Sabbaths and Festivals when there is a large gathering; however, on Monday and Thursday one may properly read before a kohen even though he is not so great — and an inference like this appears explicitly in the chapter [entitled] HaNizakin — whereas Rabbi Perida did not want to read before a kohen even on Monday and Thursday. And Rashi explained that here [the Gemara] is dealing with Grace After Meals — and so too does the wording "I did not bless" imply, since it does not say "and I did not read" — and Grace After Meals was not instituted for them on account of the ways of peace, yet even so Rabbi Perida did not want to recite the blessing before the kohen:
